title: We're making a hex tactics game where the units you kill can rise and fight for you. What would you polish first?
author: bmerrillcreative
selftext:
I'm Bryce, one of the two primary devs. I've been a game/app/website developer for 10 years and I've spent the last year+ of those on my dream game! The clip is one turn of the Veilbound, whose kills get back up and fight on their side.



You can play it free in your browser, with no download and no account for single player: [https://ritesofaccord.com/](https://ritesofaccord.com/) (on a phone it installs from the browser first, no app store).



How we use AI:

\- \*\*Code:\*\* At this point in the project, AI writes nearly all of it, client and server, I review as needed, my software engineer background does help at times. I have extensive guidelines, rules, learning, skills, pipelines, and other documentation, as well as tests, to make results reliable across different models

\- \*\*Units:\*\* each starts as a 2D painting, redrawn from more angles on Scenario, then made 3D on Meshy with the weapons made apart. Faces were a blurry mask until we started generating each head on its own and grafting it onto the body.

\- \*\*Animation:\*\* clips come from a library, or, when the library has nothing, from a short generated video of the unit's own model doing the action, tracked and put on the rig. Scripts measure every clip (twisted wrists, jerks, a weapon inside the body) and fail the build, then fresh sessions judge it blind before I see it, then I do a ton of revisions/adjustments in my custom Unit Lab until I'm happy.

\- \*\*Translation:\*\* 13 languages, held to a glossary of the game's own terms and checked by a second model.

\- \*\*Not AI:\*\* the rules, factions, lore, game design, and balance are ours, and the music and sound are by our two composers.



Happy to answer questions on any of the above and discuss further! A lot of the above learnings are pretty hard-won via trial and error.  


So my question: from the clip, or after a few minutes in the game, what would you polish first? The UI, the animation, the effects, how a turn reads, anything goes. That's what we'll work on next.
